entries.answer:
At end of turn Bronze Sable dies and Nico gets a poison counter.

Step by step:

1. Brute Strength resolves first (it was cast in response, so it's on top of the stack): Bronze Sable becomes 5/2 with trample until end of turn.
2. Virulent Wound then resolves and puts a -1/-1 counter on Bronze Sable, making it 4/1. It survives — a -1/-1 counter applies in layer 7 along with Brute Strength's +3/+1 [613.1g], and Bronze Sable's toughness is above 0, so the state-based action that would bury it doesn't apply [704.5f].
3. During the cleanup step, "until end of turn" effects expire — this is the general principle that effects lasting until the end of a step, phase, or turn wear off as that period ends [500.5a]. Brute Strength's +3/+1 goes away. Bronze Sable is back to its printed 2/1 but still has the -1/-1 counter (counters are permanent; they don't wear off), so it's 1/0.
4. With toughness 0, state-based actions put Bronze Sable into Nico's graveyard [704.5f].
5. Because Bronze Sable died this turn, Virulent Wound's delayed effect applies and Nico (its controller) gets a poison counter.

Assumption on ordering: I'm assuming Nico's Brute Strength resolves before Alma's Virulent Wound, which is forced — the later-cast spell resolves first. If instead Brute Strength had somehow resolved after the counter was already on, the end result would be identical, since the counter and the pump both just coexist until the pump expires at end of turn.

This interaction doesn't depend on player count: the outcome is the same in a two-player game or at a multiplayer table, since only Bronze Sable's controller (Nico) gets the poison counter.

entries.answer_gold: The effect from Brute Strength wears off, but the -1/-1 counter remains. Bronze Sable dies. The delayed triggered ability created by Virulent Wound is not a continuous effect, so it still exists during the cleanup step, and will trigger due to Bronze Sable dying. entries.question: Angelina controls [Ice Cauldron]. Noel controls [Suppression Field]. Angelina activates Ice Cauldron's first ability with X=1, paying {C}{C}{C}. On Angelina's next turn, they activate Ice Cauldron's second ability. How much mana do they add?

Angelina adds {C}{C}{C} — three colorless mana — and that mana can be spent only to cast the card exiled with Ice Cauldron.

Why: Ice Cauldron's first ability is an activated ability that is not a mana ability, so Suppression Field's "Activated abilities cost {2} more to activate unless they're mana abilities" applies. With X=1, the mana component became {1} plus {2} more, i.e. {3} generic in total. Angelina paid that {3} generic with three colorless mana ({C}{C}{C}) — generic costs can be paid with colorless mana. Ice Cauldron's own text tells you to "note the type and amount of mana spent to pay this activation cost," so what's noted is the mana actually spent, three colorless mana, not the {1} the printed {X} alone would have been; paying an increased cost still counts as paying the cost (118.7c/118.7d framing on cost modification, and rule 118.4 for {X} costs).

Ice Cauldron's second ability ({T}, remove a charge counter: add the last noted type and amount of mana) is a mana ability, so Suppression Field does not tax it, and it simply reproduces the noted mana: {C}{C}{C}. The restriction "Spend this mana only to cast the last card exiled with this artifact" limits how the mana can be used but does not change its type (106.6).

This works the same whether the game is two-player or multiplayer; nothing here depends on the number of opponents.

entries.answer_gold: Just {C}. The activation cost of Ice Cauldron's first ability is "{X}, {T}". The additional cost imposed by Suppression Field is not part of the activation cost, and the mana spent on it isn't noted when the ability resolves.

entries.question: Ariel activates [Warped Landscape]. Before that resolves Noe casts [Aven Mindcensor]. When Ariel is resolving Warped Landscape's ability, they find [Panglacial Wurm] in the top four cards of their library. Can they cast it?

Yes — Ariel can cast Panglacial Wurm, because it is among the four cards Ariel is actually searching.

Why: Aven Mindcensor doesn't stop the search; it replaces "search your library" with "search the top four cards of that library." Under rule 701.23f, when searching a zone is replaced with searching a portion of that zone, all other instructions that refer to searching the zone still apply. Ariel is still searching their library, just a restricted portion of it, so Panglacial Wurm's ability ("While you're searching your library, you may cast this card from your library") is live during that search. Since Panglacial Wurm is one of the top four cards Ariel is looking at, Ariel may cast it from the library right then, paying {5}{G}{G} (five generic plus two green). Nothing in rule 601.3 prohibits it.

Timeline assumption: I'm assuming Aven Mindcensor (which has flash) resolved before Warped Landscape's activated ability began resolving, as stated. If Aven Mindcensor had instead entered the battlefield after the search was already underway, it wouldn't retroactively shrink a search in progress — but either way Panglacial Wurm would be castable, and if Aven Mindcensor had restricted the search to a top four that did *not* contain Panglacial Wurm, Ariel could not cast it, since Ariel would never see it.

Other notes: casting Panglacial Wurm happens during the resolution of Warped Landscape's ability; the search then continues and finishes, and per 701.23f Ariel still shuffles their entire library, not just the four cards. If a basic land was among those four, Ariel may still put it onto the battlefield tapped.

Two players vs. multiplayer: this works the same. Aven Mindcensor's replacement applies to every opponent of Noe, so at a multiplayer table any opponent of Noe searching a library is limited to the top four cards, and each such player could likewise cast a Panglacial Wurm found there.

entries.answer_gold: Yes. Aven Mindcensor's ability is a replacement effect that replaces searching a library with searching only the top four cards of that library. However for the purposes of Panglacial Wurm's effect, it still qualifies as "searching a library".

entries.question: Addison has cast a sideboard card from [Glittering Wish], which is now in their graveyard. Addison then restarts the game with [Karn Liberated]. What happens?
entries.reason: Both answers conclude the card brought in by Glittering Wish is part of Addison's library for the restarted game (not returned to the sideboard), citing rule 727.2.
entries.answer:
The multicolored card Addison brought in from outside the game with Glittering Wish becomes part of Addison's library in the new game — it does not go back to the sideboard.

Why: once a card is brought into the game from outside the game, it's involved in that game. Rule 727.2 says all Magic cards involved in the game that was restarted are involved in the new game, even if they weren't originally involved in the restarted game, and it gives exactly this example: a player casts a wish card to bring a card in from outside the game, then the game is restarted — that card is part of that player's library when the new game begins. Ownership doesn't change regardless of where the card was when the new game starts ([727.2]), so wherever the wished-for card sat (battlefield, graveyard, stack, hand), it's shuffled into Addison's starting deck.

Glittering Wish itself is exiled by its own text, but that doesn't matter here — the question notes it's in the graveyard, and in either case every Magic card involved in the ended game is involved in the new one ([727.2]). The only exception is cards an effect specifically exempts from the restart procedure; those are not in their owner's deck as the new game begins ([727.5]). That's relevant for Karn Liberated: its −14 leaves in exile all non-Aura permanent cards exiled with Karn Liberated and then puts them onto the battlefield under Addison's control, so only those cards skip the deck. A wished-for card that wasn't exiled with Karn Liberated gets no such exemption.

Timing: the restart effect from Karn Liberated finishes resolving just before the first turn's untap step, and that's when Karn Liberated's additional instruction (putting the exiled permanent cards onto the battlefield) is carried out; no player has priority then, and any resulting triggered abilities wait until a player next receives priority, usually in the first upkeep ([727.4]).

All players still in the game when Karn Liberated restarts it begin the new game together ([104.6], [727.1]), so this works the same whether the table has two players or more; the only difference in a multiplayer game is that every remaining player is in the new game, and a new starting player is determined per the normal starting-the-game procedure.

Card data from Scryfall (scryfall.com).
entries.answer_gold: The sideboard card is shuffled into Addison's library for the restarted game.

entries.question: Alvin controls [Mycosynth Lattice], a [Dance of the Dead] attached to a [Streetbreaker Wurm] that it returned to the battlefield, and a [Mizzium Transreliquat] that is currently a copy of [Sakashima of a Thousand Faces] due to its second ability. Alvin casts [Eureka], choosing to put [March of the Machines] onto the battlefield, then putting [Copy Artifact] onto the battlefield, which copies the Mizzium Transreliquat and then copies the Dance of the Dead with its new copy ability. (The one from Sakashima of a Thousand Faces.) They choose for it to enchant a [Viashino Warrior] in their graveyard. As Eureka continues resolving, they put [Shimatsu the Bloodcloaked] onto the battlefield and sacrifice March of the Machines. After Copy Artifact's trigger resolves and returns the Viashino Warrior to the battlefield, Alvin activates the ability of the Copy Artifact to turn it into a copy of Streetbreaker Wurm. What happens?
entries.reason: The candidate concludes the Viashino will never be sacrificed (the Copy Artifact no longer has the leave-the-battlefield sacrifice-trigger), whereas the reference says the Viashino will be sacrificed if the Copy Artifact later leaves the battlefield.
entries.answer:
Direct answer: the Copy Artifact stops being a Dance of the Dead and becomes a 6/4 permanent with Streetbreaker Wurm's copiable values plus the {1}{U}{R} "becomes a copy" ability, and the Viashino Warrior is *not* sacrificed. It simply stays on the battlefield, still tapped, with no +1/+1 bonus and no untap restriction.

Step by step:

1. Because Mycosynth Lattice makes all permanents artifacts in addition to their other types, both Dance of the Dead and Streetbreaker Wurm are legal targets for the artifact-targeting copy ability, and Mycosynth Lattice also lets Alvin pay the {1}{U}{R} (one generic, one blue, one red) with mana of any color.

2. When the Copy Artifact entered as a copy of the Mizzium Transreliquat, it picked up the Transreliquat's current copiable values (Sakashima of a Thousand Faces' values, plus the {1}{U}{R} ability the Transreliquat's own exception granted it), because a copy exception's granted ability becomes part of the copiable values [707.9a], and Copy Artifact's own exception made it an enchantment in addition to its other types [707.9b].

3. When the Copy Artifact then became a copy of Dance of the Dead "except it has this ability," that change happened while it was already on the battlefield. Rule [707.4] is explicit that this kind of change does **not** cause enters-the-battlefield or leaves-the-battlefield abilities to trigger, so Dance of the Dead's "When this Aura enters..." ability should not have triggered at all, and the Copy Artifact never legitimately gained "enchant creature put onto the battlefield with this Aura" or put the Viashino Warrior onto the battlefield. I'm answering the rest as the question frames it (assuming the Viashino Warrior did get returned and the Copy Artifact was attached to it), but flag that this premise is itself contrary to [707.4].

4. Activating the ability again to copy Streetbreaker Wurm replaces the Copy Artifact's copiable values wholesale with Streetbreaker Wurm's — name Streetbreaker Wurm, Creature — Wurm, 6/4 — plus the {1}{U}{R} ability from the exception [707.3] [707.9a]. Type-changing and color effects aren't copied [707.2], but Mycosynth Lattice applies to it anew, so it is a colorless artifact creature. It is no longer an Aura and no longer has Dance of the Dead's text, so it ceases to be attached to the Viashino Warrior.

5. Critically, the Copy Artifact never leaves the battlefield — it only changes what it copies [707.4] — and it no longer has "When this Aura leaves the battlefield, that creature's controller sacrifices it." That ability therefore never triggers, and the Viashino Warrior survives.

6. The Viashino Warrior loses the +1/+1 and the "doesn't untap during its controller's untap step" clauses (those were continuous effects from the Aura's now-gone text, applied in layers 7c and elsewhere [613.6]), so it's a plain 4/2. It stays tapped, since a permanent keeps its status until something changes it [110.5c] — but it will now untap normally in Alvin's next untap step.

7. March of the Machines being sacrificed matters only in that nothing is setting noncreature artifacts' power and toughness anymore; Mycosynth Lattice alone doesn't make anything a creature. The upkeep "pay {1}{B} to untap" ability is also gone with the Dance of the Dead text.

Note on names: effects that referred to the permanent by name would still track it through the copy changes [707.11], but here nothing is left pointing at it.

This answer is the same whether the game has two players or more; Eureka's "each player" loop had already finished before any of this.

entries.question: Aspen controls a [Blood Tyrant] that they took control of from Briella using [Malevolent Whispers]. Aspen has 1 life. Cason casts [Volt Charge] targeting Aspen. After it resolves and Aspen loses the game, will Blood Tyrant get the +1/+1 counters?
entries.reason: Both answers conclude the same final ruling: the ability cannot resolve because Aspen leaves the game as they lose, so the triggered ability does not exist on the stack to give Blood Tyrant counters.
entries.answer:
Short answer: no — Blood Tyrant won't end up with the five +1/+1 counters in any practical sense.

Why:

1. The trigger does technically trigger. Blood Tyrant's "Whenever a player loses the game, put five +1/+1 counters on this creature" is one of the abilities that "looks back in time" [603.10f], and such abilities trigger whenever a player loses or leaves the game for any reason other than a draw [603.9]. Aspen at 1 life taking 3 damage from Volt Charge means Aspen has 0 or less life and loses the game as a state-based action [119.6].

2. But the controller of that triggered ability is Aspen, who is gone. In a multiplayer game, as soon as Aspen leaves, all objects Aspen owns leave the game, all control-changing effects giving Aspen control end (so Malevolent Whispers' effect ends and Blood Tyrant reverts to Briella's control), and any objects on the stack not represented by cards that Aspen controlled cease to exist [800.4a]. Blood Tyrant's triggered ability is exactly such an object — a stack object that isn't a card, controlled by Aspen at the moment it triggered — so it ceases to exist and never resolves. No counters are placed. (Blood Tyrant itself is safe: it's Briella's card, so it isn't exiled or removed; it just goes back to Briella untapped/attacking status aside, without the +2/+0 and haste from Malevolent Whispers, which also end.)

3. Two-player case: if Aspen and Cason were the only players, Aspen losing simply ends the game immediately — there's no one left to resolve Blood Tyrant's trigger, so again it contributes nothing.

Timing note: I'm assuming Volt Charge fully resolved (3 damage dealt, and its proliferate performed) before state-based actions were checked, which is the normal sequence — damage is processed into life loss as part of resolution [120.4c], and only afterward do state-based actions see Aspen at 0 or less life [119.6]. If instead you imagine Blood Tyrant somehow being back under Briella's control before the loss occurred, the trigger would be Briella's and she would get the five counters; but that isn't what happens here, since Aspen's loss and Aspen's departure are the same event.

Card data from Scryfall (scryfall.com).
entries.answer_gold: No. As Aspen loses the game, the effect granting them control of Blood Tyrant ends, and it returns to Briella. "Loses the game" triggers use the game state immediately before they triggered to determine how that trigger is handled. Since Aspen controlled Blood Tyrant right before losing the game, the trigger would be placed onto the stack under their control. However Aspen is no longer in the game when the trigger would be placed onto the stack, so it never is.

entries.question: Aspen, Brycen, and Collins begin a multiplayer game. In Aspen's upkeep, they use [Leyline of Anticipation], several [Simian Spirit Guide]s and [Desperate Ritual]s, and [Goblin Charbelcher] to kill Brycen. Does Aspen draw a card for the turn?
entries.reason: The candidate reaches the same correct conclusion and reasoning as the reference: because the game began multiplayer the starting player doesn't skip their first draw and killing Brycen doesn't end or interrupt Aspen's turn, so Aspen will draw.
entries.answer:
Yes. Aspen draws a card in their draw step.

Two points make this clear:

entries.question: Avery controls [Caelorna, Coral Tyrant] and [Darksteel Garrison] that's fortifying [Spire Garden]. Avery casts [Bludgeon Brawl]. Spider Umbra is destroyed and Mons's Goblin Raiders remains on the battlefield.

The "move to the graveyard" event is a part of the "destroy" event, so the umbra armor replacement effect must apply first. Once that effect has been applied, the creature is no longer about to die, so there are no more effects to apply.

entries.question: Abel attacks with [Pristine Angel]. While it's tapped, Nico activates [Cephalid Snitch]'s ability targeting Pristine Angel. After that resolves, Abel casts a spell and untaps Pristine Angel. Can Nico now target the Pristine Angel with [Murder]?

entries.question: At the beginning of the game, Alex announced [Kaheera, the Orphanguard] as their companion. During the game, Alex cast [Carrion Grub] from their sideboard with [Wish]. Later, Alex restarts the game with [Karn Liberated]. What happens?

entries.answer:

Details:

1. Restart itself: Karn Liberated's −14 ability ends the current game immediately; no one wins, loses, or draws it, and all players who were in the game start a new game using the normal starting-the-game procedure [727.1], [104.6]. The restart effect finishes resolving just before the first turn's untap step, and Karn Liberated's additional instruction (leaving the exiled non-Aura permanent cards in exile, then putting them onto the battlefield under Alex's control) is carried out at that time. No player has priority then, so anything that triggers — for example Carrion Grub's "when this creature enters, mill four cards" if Carrion Grub happened to be one of those cards — goes on the stack the next time a player gets priority, usually in the first turn's upkeep step [727.4].

Carrion Grub, cast off Wish from outside the game: every Magic card involved in the ended game is involved in the new game, even cards that weren't originally part of it, and ownership doesn't change. A card brought in from outside the game this way is part of its owner's library when the new game begins [727.2]. So Carrion Grub (assuming it is not among the cards exiled with Karn Liberated) is in Alex's starting library for the new game. Cards that an effect exempts from the restart procedure — here, the non-Aura permanent cards exiled with Karn Liberated — are not in their owner's deck as the new game begins [727.5], [727.5a].

3. Kaheera, the Orphanguard: if Alex had already paid {3} to put Kaheera, the Orphanguard into hand from outside the game, it stays in the game until the game ends [702.139c], and by [727.2] it likewise becomes part of Alex's library in the new game (again unless it was exiled with Karn Liberated). If Alex never took that special action, Kaheera, the Orphanguard was still outside the game and the provided rules don't state that it joins the new game.

What the provided rules do NOT settle: whether Alex still has Kaheera, the Orphanguard available as a companion in the restarted game, and whether the presence of Carrion Grub (an Insect, not a Cat/Elemental/Nightmare/Dinosaur/Beast) in the new game's starting deck breaks the companion condition. The only companion rule given is [702.139b], which says "starting deck" means your deck after setting aside sideboard cards — it doesn't address restarted games. Treat that part as unresolved by this context.

5. Multiplayer: the same answer applies with more than two players — all players in the game when it ended start the new game [727.1], and in a game using the limited range of influence option every player is involved regardless of the range of influence of Karn Liberated's controller [727.7].

entries.question: Alex controls a [Krark-Clan Ironworks], a [Mycosynth Lattice], and a [Control Magic] that took control of a [Boris Devilboon] from Nico. Alex begins activating the ability of Boris Devilboon and sacrifices Control Magic to help pay the cost. Is this legal? If so, who will control the ability?

entries.answer:
Yes, it's legal, and Alex controls the activated ability of Boris Devilboon.

Why it's legal:
- Only an object's controller may activate its activated ability, and that's checked when the activation begins [602.2], [701.2a]. At that moment Control Magic ("You control enchanted creature") is applying in the control-changing layer [613.1b], so Alex is the controller of Boris Devilboon and may legally begin activating {2}{B}{R}, {T}.
- During the payment step Alex may activate mana abilities. Mycosynth Lattice makes all permanents artifacts, so Control Magic is an artifact and can be sacrificed to Krark-Clan Ironworks to add {C}{C}. Mycosynth Lattice also says players may spend mana as though it were mana of any color, so that {C}{C} can pay the {B} and the {R} of Boris Devilboon's cost. The remaining {2} generic can be paid with any mana, and the {T} is paid by tapping Boris Devilboon.
- Nothing rewinds the activation when Control Magic leaves the battlefield: announcements and payments can't be altered once made, and the activation is only rewound if a player can't complete a step of activation [602.2]. Losing control of the source mid-payment isn't such a failure.

Who controls the ability: the controller of an activated ability on the stack is the player who activated it [113.8]. That's Alex. Timing note: I'm assuming Alex sacrifices Control Magic while paying costs for the already-announced ability. If instead Alex sacrificed Control Magic first and only then tried to announce the ability, the activation would be illegal — Boris Devilboon would already be Nico's, and Alex couldn't begin activating it [602.2], [701.2a].

Player count doesn't matter here: the same answer holds in a two-player game or at a multiplayer table.

entries.answer_gold:
Yes, this is legal, and Alex will control the ability. The process for activating an ability is the same as the process for casting a spell. The first step of activating an ability is to put it onto the stack. Mana abilities are activated in a later step. The ability is already on the stack at this point (controlled by Alex), so the Boris Devilboon changing controllers won't change who controls the ability. After activating mana abilities, Alex must pay the activation cost. {T} means "tap this permanent", so Alex can pay the cost regardless of who controls the Boris Devilboon at that time.

Legality is checked before mana abilities are activated, so it won't matter that Boris Devilboon gets summoning sickness when it changes controllers.

entries.question: Nico has cast a [Gather Specimens] earlier in the turn. Aiden controls a [Chronatog Totem] that is currently a creature due to its own ability, and casts an [Evil Twin], choosing to have it copy Chronatog Totem. What happens?

Other effects — including type-changing effects — are not copied [707.2]. Chronatog Totem's own {1}{U} ability making it a 1/2 blue Atog artifact creature is exactly such a type-changing effect, so Evil Twin does not copy the "is currently a creature" part. It copies Chronatog Totem as a plain artifact with the {T}: Add {U} ability, the {1}{U} animation ability, and the {0} +3/+3 ability, plus the Evil Twin exception ability "{U}{B}, {T}: Destroy target creature with the same name as this creature," which becomes part of its copiable values [707.9a][707.9b].

Even if Gather Specimens were considered first, the object that actually enters is a noncreature artifact, so Gather Specimens' condition isn't met.

He can pay {1}{U} to animate it into a 1/2 blue Atog artifact creature, and then, with the Evil Twin ability, pay {U}{B} and tap it to destroy target creature with the same name — which could be Aiden's original Chronatog Totem, if it's still a creature (the ability targets a creature with the same name).

entries.question: Albert and Nico are beginning the game and have just drawn 7 cards. Albert has [Serum Powder] in their hand. Does Albert get to know whether Nico is going to mulligan before deciding whether to use Serum Powder's ability?

entries.answer:
It depends on who declares first. Serum Powder's ability works "any time you could mulligan," which means Albert may use it at the moment Albert would declare whether to take a mulligan. Mulligan declarations are made in turn order, beginning with the starting player, and all mulligans are then taken simultaneously [103.5b].

- If Albert is the starting player, Albert declares first, so Albert must decide about exiling their hand to Serum Powder before knowing whether Nico will mulligan.

If Albert does use it, Albert exiles all cards in hand and draws that many, then declares whether to take a mulligan.

What Albert never learns in advance is the *content* of Nico's new hand — only whether Nico declared a mulligan, and only if Nico declared first.

Declarations go in turn order from the starting player [103.5b], so Albert knows the declarations of every player who declares before Albert and none of those after. In a multiplayer game (and Brawl), the first mulligan doesn't count toward cards bottomed or mulligans allowed [103.5c], and with shared team turns teammates may consult and a player may mulligan even after a teammate has kept [805.3a].

Yes — Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is a creature, and its only creature type is Elemental (it is a green 6/4 Elemental creature that is still a legendary land with the land types it had plus Swamp).
